title: BCA Investigation: First Report
notebook: 840 million kroner of Halvek-era contracts went to his inner circle. Patronage, not bids.
Thirty-four people profited. Twelve sit in parliament. Four hold posts in my government.
Maren wants the audit to cover the eighteen months after Halvek's resignation.
location: Bureau of Civic Accountability Headquarters — Ashenmere

narrative.text: The BCA headquarters occupies the second floor of a former Halvek-era tax office — a building that Maren Tovik selected deliberately. 'Every bureaucrat who walks in here will remember what this building used to be,' she told you at the opening. 'That memory is worth more than a new paint job.' Six months in, the paint is still peeling, but the investigation boards on the walls are covered in names, dates, and connecting lines that tell a story about where the Halvek regime's money went.

Chancellor. We have completed our initial audit of Halvek-era procurement contracts. The findings are substantial. Between 1954 and 1962 — the final eight years of the regime — approximately 840 million kroner in state contracts were awarded to companies linked to Halvek's inner circle. These were not competitive bids. They were patronage. The money flowed through eighteen shell corporations, seven of which are still operating under different names. We have identified thirty-four individuals who personally profited. Twelve are currently serving in parliament. Four hold positions in your government.
She pauses. The pause is significant. Maren Tovik does not pause for dramatic effect. She pauses when she is about to say something that will make the room feel different.

I have not yet determined whether any of those four are in this room. I am informing you of that uncertainty because transparency requires it, not because I have evidence of wrongdoing by anyone in your immediate circle. The investigation is ongoing. I will report again when the scope narrows. In the meantime, I am requesting authorization to expand the audit to include the period of transition — the eighteen months between Halvek's resignation and your election. That period had minimal oversight. The records are fragmentary. If corruption occurred, that is where it happened.

Four people in my government. She did not say which four. She did not say whether I am one of them. She does not know yet — or she knows and she is waiting until she has enough evidence to tell me without ambiguity. Either way, Maren Tovik is doing exactly what I asked her to do: investigating corruption wherever it leads. The fact that it might lead here is not a flaw in the system. It is the system working. I have to decide whether I actually believe that — or whether I only believed it until the investigation got close.

monologue: Four people in my government. She did not say which four. Tovik does not pause for dramatic effect — she paused because she was about to say something that would make the room feel different. The investigation is working exactly as designed. The question is whether I meant it when I said I wanted corruption investigated wherever it leads — or whether 'wherever' stopped at my own doorstep.

choices.text: "Expand the audit to cover the transition period. Full access to whatever records survive. If corruption happened during those eighteen months, I want to know — regardless of who it implicates. Maren, you have my authorization to follow the evidence wherever it leads. If it leads to people in this government, they will be held accountable like anyone else. That is not a threat. It is a promise — to the people who voted for a government that would be different from the one it replaced."

reactions.text: She writes the authorization on her notepad — full access, wherever it leads. Her pen does not hesitate. She has been waiting for you to say the words. Now she will act on them.

choices.text: "Audit the transition period, but with restrictions. Focus on contracts above 500,000 kroner — the kind of money that indicates systemic corruption rather than administrative sloppiness. And I want to be briefed before any findings related to current government officials are made public. Not to suppress information, but to ensure that I am not blindsided by a report I could have been prepared for. Transparency matters. So does stability. I am trying to balance both."

reactions.text: She writes limited scope on her notepad — contracts above 500,000. She does not argue. The silence is the sound of Maren Tovik accepting a restriction while filing it away for later reference.

choices.text: "Focus on the cases you have already identified. Prosecute the twelve parliamentarians — that will send the strongest possible signal that the old corruption is over. The transition period was chaotic. Opening that door means dragging this government through investigations of decisions made under emergency conditions, by people who were trying to hold the country together. I am not protecting corruption. I am protecting the transition government's legacy — which includes my own election. If the BCA audits the transition, every political opponent I have will use those findings to delegitimize this administration."

reactions.text: She closes her notebook. The motion is slow and deliberate. She does not argue. The silence is the sound of Maren Tovik recalculating the limits of her mandate.
